actions.body: Autonomous systems increasingly rely on memory-dependent components that influence how agents process environmental feedback [source-e47ad9c78a9a44dd]. These components are not passive storage; they are active elements that mediate interaction with dynamic environments, such as in physical simulations where state-history constrains movement [source-cd7c979e3e904a7e]. This integration suggests that experiential history acts as a filter, potentially narrowing the range of future value acquisition by biasing the agent toward specific previously-rewarded state-action paths [source-ef971ce280a64c52].
actions.lede: Memory architectures in autonomous agents do not merely record; they shape the future trajectory of value optimization.
